'''Evert Ingolf Lindau''' (born 4 October 1942) is a Swedish physicist and professor emeritus at [[Lund University]] and [[Stanford University]] and a member of the [[Royal Swedish Academy of Sciences]].

== Biography ==

Lindau was awarded his [[PhD]] in 1971 at [[Chalmers University of Technology]] with his [[dissertation]] about photoemission and optical absorption studies of the band structure.<ref>{{Cite book|title=Photoemission and optical absorption studies of the band structure and plasmon excitations in metallic systems|last=Lindau|first=Ingolf|publisher=|year=1971|isbn=|series=|location=Gothenburg|pages=}}</ref> After the dissertation, he began working at the Silicon Valley–based company [[Varian Associates]] in [[Palo Alto, California|Palo Alto]] between 1971 and 1972 before he was employed at Stanford University in 1972.<ref name=":0" /> In 1973 he obtained the first X-ray photoemission spectra of the 4''f'' levels of [[gold]].<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Doniach|first1=S.|last2=Hodgson|first2=K.|last3=Lindau|first3=I.|last4=Pianetta|first4=P.|last5=Winick|first5=H.|date=1997-11-01|title=Early Work with Synchrotron Radiation at Stanford|url=https://scripts.iucr.org/cgi-bin/paper?S0909049597012235|journal=Journal of Synchrotron Radiation|language=en|volume=4|issue=6|pages=380–395|doi=10.1107/s0909049597012235|pmid=16699252|bibcode=1997JSynR...4..380D |issn=0909-0495}}</ref> In 1980 he became a professor at Stanford University for his research in electrical engineering and photonics.<ref name=":0" /> During his professorships he took a [[sabbatical]] at [[Lund University]] between 1988 and 1989, where he worked at [[MAX Lab]] to expand its research facility. After his sabbatical ended he return to Lund University to become a professor for his research in [[Synchrotron light|synchrotron light physics]].<ref>{{Cite book|title=Fysik i Lund: i tid och rum|last=|first=|publisher=Fysiska institutionen i samarbete med Gidlunds förlag|year=2016|isbn=978-91-7844-972-9|editor-last=Forkman|editor-first=Bengt|location=Lund|pages=401–402|language=Swedish|editor-last2=Holmin|editor-first2=Verdozzi Kristina}}</ref> In 1991, Lindau succeeded Bengt Forkman as director of the Max Lab. As a director, he was in charge of the creation of the second accelerator for [[synchrotron radiation]] research in MAX Lab.<ref>{{Cite book|title=MAX-lab i förklarat ljus: från Ur-MAX till MAX IV|last=|first=|publisher=MAX IV|year=2016|isbn=978-91-7623-679-6|editor-last=Forkman|editor-first=Bengt|location=Lund|page=31|language=Swedish|editor-last2=Nyberg|editor-first2=Annika|editor-last3=Nygren|editor-first3=Mats}}</ref>

His research has focused on studies of electronic properties of semiconductor surfaces and their boundary layers using synchrotron light.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web|url=http://simes.stanford.edu/investigator/ingolf-lindau-2/|title=SIMES » » Ingolf Lindau|website=simes.stanford.edu|language=en-US|access-date=2017-05-01|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170228081304/http://simes.stanford.edu/investigator/ingolf-lindau-2/|archive-date=2017-02-28}}</ref> He has also contributed to the production and development of instruments used in synchrotron light systems, both at [[SLAC National Accelerator Laboratory|SLAC]] and at [[Stanford Synchrotron Radiation Lightsource]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www6.slac.stanford.edu/news/2013-08-16-Seminar-Honors-Ingolf-Lindau.aspx|title=Seminar Honors Ingolf Lindau|website=SLAC National Accelerator Laboratory|language=en|access-date=2017-05-23}}</ref> He was elected as a member of the Royal Swedish Academy of Sciences as the 1402th member.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.kva.se/sv/om-oss/ledamoter/ingolf-lindau|title=Ingolf Lindau|last=|first=|date=|website=Kungliga Vetenskapsakademien|access-date=2017-05-23}}</ref>
